explanation: Find the end of the first half, reverse the second half, and compare corresponding nodes. Reverse the second half again before returning so the original list links are restored. The middle node of an odd-length list needs no comparison.
timeComplexity: O(n) time. Midpoint discovery, reversal, comparison and restoration are each linear.
spaceComplexity: O(1) auxiliary space. Reversal and scans use a constant number of node pointers.
attribution: Original C# implementation and explanation authored for EPI Practice from the displayed problem contract.
correctness: After reversing the second half, its order equals the original suffix read backward. Comparing it with the prefix therefore checks every mirrored pair; an odd middle value needs no comparison. Reversing it again restores the exact original links before returning.
walkthrough: For [8,3,6,3,8], split after the middle 6 and reverse [3,8] to [8,3]. Those values match the first two nodes. Restore [3,8] and return true.
edgeCases: Empty and singleton lists are palindromes.
Odd-length lists skip the unmatched middle node.
Restore the second half even when a mismatch was found.
